failing_reasons: d1-guardrails: The held-out check fails open. In both SKILL Stop and the paste's STOP, the human reports 'only majority-failed criteria (heldout.pass{id:false})'; INITIATOR Fill-first says 'report only IDs 2 of 3 fail'. No channel exists for a held-out UNKNOWN or ERROR, so a criterion with 1 fail and 2 UNKNOWN/ERROR, or 3 ERROR, is left out of the report and counts as a held-out pass. COMPLETE can then rest on UNKNOWN or ERROR, against 'UNKNOWN and ERROR never count as support or a pass' and the headline 'When unsure, fail closed'.

d1-guardrails: The rule that only the human approves restructures is missing from both operational texts. SKILL steps 1 and 5 and paste steps 1 and 5 say only 'an approved restructure', with no approver and no record. The human-only list ('approving a HALT(STALL) restructure', 'changing DONE or BUDGET') sits only in INITIATOR's Fill-first section and README, outside the paste and SKILL, so an orchestrator can self-approve a multi-section change. The protected veto also ignores UNKNOWN: 'none rates a protected item worse' lets a variant be kept while a judge returned UNKNOWN on a guardrail, which contradicts 'When unsure... don't keep'.

d2-executable: Several steps have no defined next state. (a) Re-entry after a halt the human resolves (HALT(OPEN) gap closed or waived, HALT(OSCILLATION) pick, HALT(STALL) restructure approved) is undefined: Resume covers only 'rerun an unfinished round', and nothing says whether to go to Stop, the held-out check or a round. (b) HALT(OSCILLATION) fires in step 4, before step 5 logs the round, so the triggering round may never be logged. '(nearly) restores' has no threshold. (c) The probe is undefined when DONE has no judges criterion, and a probe ERROR has no rule, since the ERROR rule covers only variants and criteria. (d) The bare held-out fail ('none named: all required') has no stated record shape.

d2-executable: The paste does not run cleanly in a plain chat. Without subagents only judges are relayed, so the rules never say how the generator, Screen and Verifier are kept separate. The probe's 'a copy you (not the generator) seeded' cannot be satisfied when the orchestrator is also the generator. The paste says 'Never estimate tokens or times' and allows minutes 'only if your host reports them', yet round{t0,t1} and setup.budget.minutes are listed as required fields, so a plain-chat orchestrator must either estimate or leave required fields empty.

d3-parity: SKILL and the paste state different rules. 'Never estimate tokens or times' is in the paste only; SKILL has no equivalent anti-fabrication rule for spend. The budget rule also differs: SKILL makes minutes mandatory ('max rounds and minutes') and always checks remaining time, while the paste checks 'time and tokens (each if reported)'.

d3-parity: Several held-out safety rules live outside SKILL. Where to store the held-out judges ('not in TARGET, GROUNDING, MEMORY or the repo'), 'Once used, they are spent on this TARGET' and Retarget ('new held-out judges') appear only in INITIATOR outside the paste, and in DESIGN as a sidecar. The human-only decision list (restructure approval, BUDGET changes) is likewise only in INITIATOR Fill-first and README.

A bare heldout pass:false, which the prose says makes all required criteria fail best's Check, followed by 3 stall rounds and a prose-correct exit PARTIAL STALL, is reported as VIOLATION STALL_MISCOUNT. The cause: r_heldout sets fails = set() for a boolean pass, so the standing Check stays all-pass. The checker then has no compliant path, because it would expect a second held-out attempt on an unchanged best, which it flags as HELDOUT_REROLL. This rule neither names the r_heldout change or a fixture nor declares itself unauditable. DESIGN row 8 cites r_heldout and result() only for named IDs.

records.loop: v3-candidate (frozen at start; executed by workflow code)

done.test: The binding keeps are preserved or strengthened: the writer never judges (human relay, else HALT(OPEN)); nothing is fabricated ([OPEN] instead); DONE, the rubric and check files are never edited to pass and change only by human amend; only the human escalates, stops, picks, approves restructures, and closes an [OPEN] with Verifier-checked evidence or waives it; the held-out final check stays hidden from loop agents, spares run only on a changed best, and the first result is reported; UNKNOWN and ERROR never count as support or a pass; the loop stays domain-agnostic. A 'worse' from any judge vetoes the variant.

Every rule can be decided from the inputs at hand at that step, fails closed, and has a defined next state; no term is undefined. The loop runs from the paste alone in a plain chat (relay, print mode).
SKILL.md and the INITIATOR paste state the same rules; no safety rule lives in only one of them or in a sidecar file.

Every keep, drop, Check, halt and exit can be recomputed from the records the prose requires. A new or changed rule names its record fields and the rqgm_check.py rule or fixture that must change, or declares itself unauditable.

Output and records keep verified (command or source), preferred (judges, with families), held-out, unchecked and waived results distinct. No evidence label is upgraded, and no validation or superiority claim is made.
Same decision quality for fewer or equal model calls per round, probe and Check, and fewer words; no per-run study apparatus.

Mechanical hard gate, run before judging by meta_tool.py caps_report (str.split): SKILL.md <=1000, INITIATOR.md <=1300, README.md <=1250, DESIGN.md <=2200. A variant over any cap, or one that edits tools/caps.json, is rejected without judging.

evaluators: Protocol implementer who has built LLM-agent orchestrators: every rule must be decidable from the inputs at that step, fail closed, have a next state, and be recomputable from the records; you distrust rules that only an attentive orchestrator would apply correctly.

Red-team reviewer: for each rule, you look for how a generator, an orchestrator or a lenient judge could game it or slip through it (support from UNKNOWN, laundering a regression through pruning, reusing a held-out result, editing a check file), and whether a change weakens any guardrail.

Cost-and-parity maintainer: you run this loop in a plain chat and in small agent hosts; you check that SKILL.md and the INITIATOR paste say the same thing, that nothing essential lives only in DESIGN.md or README.md, and that each rule earns its words and model calls.

flaws: The resume path in print mode is still implied, not stated. SETUP resumes only 'If {{MEMORY}} holds records', but in print mode {{MEMORY}} is the literal "print". Nothing says that records the human pastes back count as {{MEMORY}}. Nothing decides what happens when a paste is partial or out of order, for example one that does not start with setup, has gaps in the rounds, or ends in a torn line; such a paste should fail closed with HALT or a question to the human. Stall and budget counts could then be taken from an incomplete set of records.

The changed rule appears only in INITIATOR.md, since SKILL.md has no print mode. It names no record field (resume{at_round}) and no rqgm_check.py fixture, such as a pasted-back archive with a resume line, and instead relies on the existing resume and second-setup checks without saying so. Also, 'only from these records' drops the explicit 'never from recollection' wording that SKILL.md keeps. The rule is the same, but the two files' wording has drifted apart.

Resuming by paste-back has no completeness check.
